name: Idaho Regional Travel and Convention (ITC) Grant Program
funder: Idaho Department of Commerce / Idaho Travel Council

geography.region: Statewide, allocated to seven travel regions by where the 2% lodging tax was collected

award: No minimum; maximum is the region's share of 2% lodging tax collections. 2026 cycle awarded $11,155,592 to 24 organizations (largest: Yellowstone Teton Territory $2,064,539; Visit Boise $1,847,022; Coeur d'Alene CVB $1,330,000; SWITA $1,258,331). Awards of $100,000+ require an independent compliance audit.

deadlines.label: 2026 cycle application close, 4:30 p.m. MT (grant period Aug 1, 2026 to Sept 30, 2027) (passed)

opens: 2027 cycle not yet posted; 2026 cycle opened Feb 5 and closed March 30, 2025 cycle opened Feb 2 and closed March 31 with presentations in May and awards at the late-July council meeting
match: 12.5% cash match documented by actual exchange of money from the applicant or partners; higher match viewed favorably (2025 guidelines)
notes: Funded by Idaho's 2% statewide lodging tax. Applicants must be incorporated nonprofits with a viable travel or convention promotion program; preference to destination marketing organizations promoting overnight visitation. Eligible uses include advertising, familiarization tours, sponsorship of major events and partnerships, trade shows, PR and research; entertainment, alcohol and honoraria are not eligible. Festivals rarely apply directly; the practical route is to ask the regional grantee (Visit Boise, Coeur d'Alene CVB, YTT, SWITA, Twin Falls Area Chamber, Southeast Idaho High Country Tourism, Sun Valley Marketing Alliance, Hailey Chamber, Stanley-Sawtooth Chamber, Greater Pocatello CVB, Visit Lewis Clark Valley, Moscow Chamber, Greater Sandpoint Chamber, Post Falls Chamber, McCall Area Chamber, Nampa Chamber, LCEDA, Challis Chamber, Bear Lake Valley CVB, NCITA, North Alliance) for event sponsorship from their ITC budget.

McCall Area Chamber of Commerce & Visitors Bureau

name: Entry Track
funder: Idaho Commission on the Arts (Arts Idaho)
award: Varies; set by formula weighing panel assessment, organization fiscal size and past Commission funding. Program-wide, Arts Idaho's FY2026 annual grants totaled nearly $750,000 to 108 organizations and schools.

notes: Annual operating-style support for arts nonprofits and university arts programs, and the required first step before Public Programs in the Arts. Requires 501(c)(3) determination letter dated at least three years before the deadline (or a unit of local, county, tribal or state government), a SAM.gov UEI, three years of program history, payment of professional artists, and arts as the nonprofit's primary purpose. Arts Idaho says it is restructuring grant opportunities, so check the site before applying.

name: Public Programs in the Arts (PPA)
funder: Idaho Commission on the Arts (Arts Idaho)
award: Varies; formula based on panel review, fiscal size and funding history

deadlines.label: FY2028 annual deadline (year three of the 2025-2027 three-year review cycle)

opens: Open now; applications due each January, review in April, final report due July 31
notes: Annual support for established professional arts organizations (three-year track record, paid professional artists and administrators, arts as primary purpose). Organizations enter only after at least one year of Entry Track funding and staff notification of PPA status. 2025 was a full panel year; 2026 and 2027 use interim staff review.

name: Arts Education Annual Projects
funder: Idaho Commission on the Arts (Arts Idaho)
award: Up to $10,000; awards depend on panel scores and available funds
opens: Open now; projects must begin after July 1, 2027
match: 1:1 cash or in-kind; grant covers no more than 50% of projected expenses
notes: Projects uniting schools, artists and community organizations in arts learning. Nonprofits need a 501(c)(3) letter effective at least one year before the deadline and one year of Idaho operations; schools, districts and units of government are eligible. A festival with a school residency or youth workshop component fits here.

name: QuickFunds / Quarterly Grants for Organizations (not currently listed)
funder: Idaho Commission on the Arts (Arts Idaho)
award: Historically up to $1,100 per quarterly project grant (2024 listings)
opens: No quarterly deadlines posted; the grants page currently lists only the January 31, 2027 annual programs and says Arts Idaho is restructuring grant opportunities
notes: Arts Idaho's small quarterly project grants (marketed as QuickFunds and later as quarterly Projects grants for organizations, informal groups through a fiscal agent, and schools) paid up to about $1,100 and notified applicants about three weeks after each deadline. The 2026 grant guidelines still describe quarterly-grant rules but no quarterly opportunity is listed on the site as of Nov 2026; treat as paused and ask staff whether a small-project track will return.

name: Major Grants
award: Up to $4,000 (board may reduce requests)

FY2027 final draft application; board review February 2027

notes: Impact areas include arts and culture and quality of life (community spaces); project types include new or expanded programs, capital and equipment, and capacity building. name: First Federal Foundation Grants
funder: First Federal Foundation (First Federal Bank, Twin Falls)

geography.region: Southern Idaho: Magic Valley, Mini-Cassia and Treasure Valley

award: Generally $1,000 to $5,000 for capital projects
opens: Two cycles a year; summer cycle closes before the July board meeting (date not posted)
notes: Capital grants for educational, civic, health, human services, social and cultural organizations; equipment such as sound systems, staging or AEDs for a festival qualifies. Individuals, political causes, religious organizations and private clubs are not funded.

name: YTT Tourism Grant (marketing and event sponsorship)

geography.region: Idaho Travel Region 6 (eastern Idaho)

award: Not published per award; funded from YTT's ITC grant ($2,064,539 in 2026, $1.92 million in 2025)
opens: 2027-28 cycle expected to open in early 2027 with a February deadline; YTT membership ($100 a year) gives applicants more say in spending
notes: Businesses and organizations in the six counties apply for marketing support and event sponsorships that show heads-in-beds return. YTT also runs a cash match program with partners and trade-show booth co-ops. Dates come from Post Register and East Idaho News coverage of the 2026 call; confirm on the YTT site.

name: Small Community Advertising and Brochure Co-Op Programs
funder: Southeast Idaho High Country Tourism (Region 5 travel council)

geography.region: Idaho Travel Region 5 (southeast Idaho)

award: Up to $2,500 per community per year (advertising co-op), covering up to 50% of cost
opens: Requests due by the January HCT meeting each year; projects completed by September 30
notes: Members partner with HCT on out-of-region advertising, including event promotion, and on printing community brochures. The local HCT member must submit the request. Funded by HCT's ITC grant ($240,157 in 2025).

name: Event and Sports Event Sponsorships
funder: Visit Boise (Boise Metro Chamber of Commerce)
contact: Lucas Gebhart, Associate Director of Sports Sales, 208-472-5204, lgebhart@visitboise.com; Julia Carroll, 208-472-5237, jcarroll@visitboise.com

geography.region: Boise and Visit Boise partner-hotel market

award: Not published; scored on economic impact, partner-hotel room nights and media exposure
opens: Submit the Sports Event or Other Event Sponsorship Form 9 to 12 months before the event; funds are budgeted a year ahead
notes: Funded mostly by Visit Boise's ITC grant ($1,847,022 in 2026). The best-matched Idaho sponsorship program for an overnight-driving festival or glow in the Treasure Valley; a post-event survey is required.

name: Community Event Sponsorship Program
funder: City of Boise, Office of Community Engagement

geography.region: Boise city limits

award: Not published
opens: Apply via cityofboise.jotform.com/form/sponsorship-request; allow at least six weeks for review and contact the city early in planning
notes: Sponsorships for free, broadly accessible events organized by nonprofits, public agencies or community groups in Boise that highlight local culture and align with city goals. Ticketed galas, fundraisers, private and invitation-only events are not funded; a free public glow would qualify, a ticketed one would not.

name: Arts and History Annual Grant
funder: City of Boise, Department of Arts and History
contact: Makenzi Dunstan, Grants and Outreach Manager, mdunstan@cityofboise.org, 208-608-7793

geography.region: Programming in Boise by applicants based in Ada, Boise, Canyon, Elmore or Gem County

award: $1,000 to $5,000 in $500 increments from a $150,000 pool (FY27)
opens: FY2028 cycle expected to open around May 1, 2027 (FY27 opened May 1 and closed June 16)
match: Grant may not exceed 50% of total project expenses
notes: Project grants for individuals, organizations and community groups offering arts, history or cultural programming in Boise. Government agencies and groups already receiving significant in-kind city support are ineligible. Final report due within 30 days of the project.

name: Energize A.C.T. (Activate, Connect, Transform) Neighborhood Grants
funder: City of Boise, Energize Our Neighborhoods

geography.region: Boise recognized neighborhood associations

award: Up to $2,500 per neighborhood association per fiscal year

deadlines.label: Winter 2027 cycle (Jan 1 to Feb 28; funding April 1)

opens: Winter cycle accepts applications January 1 to February 28; summer cycle July 1 to August 31
notes: Only recognized Boise neighborhood associations may apply, but the Celebration category pays for block parties, picnics and neighborhood festivals including entertainment, sound equipment and park permit fees. An event producer partners with the association as the applicant. Projects must be on public property within city limits.

name: Art Spotlight CDA: Performing Arts Grant
funder: City of Coeur d'Alene Arts Commission
contact: Jo Anne Mateski, City Staff Support to the Arts Commission (email on program page)

geography.region: Kootenai County-based performing arts nonprofits

award: $5,000 or $7,500 from a $15,000 annual pool, with a possible second-year payment

deadlines.label: 2025-26 cycle, 5 p.m. PT (year one Nov 2025 to Oct 2026) (passed)

opens: 2026-27 performing arts deadline not posted on the program page; the companion Visual Arts round closed July 10, 2026
notes: For 501(c)(3)s with at least five years of performing arts programming that regularly present artists to general audiences. Applications submitted by email with the subject line specified on the page.

name: Art Spotlight CDA: Visual Arts Grant
funder: City of Coeur d'Alene Arts Commission
contact: City of Coeur d'Alene Arts Commission staff

geography.region: Coeur d'Alene

award: $5,000 or $7,500 per project from a $15,000 pool, with possible second-year support
opens: Next round expected summer 2027
notes: Exhibitions, educational programs, public art, youth arts, workshops and collaborative community arts projects, with priority on K-12 opportunities. Reviewed on artistic quality, community engagement, feasibility and public impact.

name: Small Local Grants (quarterly)

geography.region: Pocatello area

award: Not published; funding is limited and one grant per recipient per fiscal year
opens: Next cycle (for January 2027 consideration) expected around December 20, 2026 per the prior-year pattern; not yet posted
notes: Visual, literary and performance art projects with clear benefit to Pocatello, including bringing in outside artists. For-profits qualify only for not-for-profit public-benefit projects. Murals accepted only in cycles 2 and 3. Final report due within six months.

name: Municipal Powers Outsource Grants (MPOG)

geography.region: Twin Falls

award: Up to $10,000 per organization; all-or-nothing awards

deadlines.label: FY2027 round (May 30 per the program page's annual timeline; confirm)

opens: Council scoring in early June; MPOG meeting the following week
notes: Grants to local nonprofits and government units delivering a municipal power under Idaho Code Title 50 Chapter 3 tied to a city Strategic Plan goal. Past examples are senior services; a community event serving a city goal (parks and recreation, cultural programming) can be argued.
